For those considering switching from Windows to Mac, the software limitations they face are actually quite few. Not only can all the largest PC applications run on the Mac platform, but there are also tens of thousands of practical applications exclusive to Mac.

The biggest exception is gaming. However, the latest tests show that, whether through official or unofficial means, Windows games now perform better than ever on Mac……

Apple has launched a dedicated game porting toolkit to help developers evaluate how their Windows games run on Mac, thereby encouraging and facilitating the porting of games to the Mac platform.

However, Filipe Esposito from Macworld pointed out that this tool has also been used by gamers to run Windows software on Mac unofficially. He himself is one of them, and stated that the latest beta version has brought significant performance improvements, citing Grand Theft Auto V as an example.

After testing the Game Porting Toolkit 4 beta for several days on a MacBook Pro equipped with the M4 Pro chip, I found that the performance improvements fundamentally transformed the experience of running demanding Windows games…… Using the same 24GB M4 Pro MacBook Pro, identical game settings, and the same benchmark, the frame rate of GTA V jumped from approximately 106 fps under GPTK 3 to around 176 fps with the GPTK 4 beta—an increase of about 66%. The game ran very smoothly at 2K resolution with medium to high settings.

He acknowledged that not every game sees such dramatic results, but he hopes these advances will encourage game studios to consider Mac as a viable platform.
